about: What each FDT firmware version does that a host has to know before it talks to it. A capability holds from its 'since' version until a later entry with the same id; a version before 1.2.8.0, or one that cannot be read (the vendor's '001.002.003'), gets 'unknown'. Facts come from the firmware line; this file is hosted by the Cloud and copied into Android and the SDK.

evidence_words.measured: seen on an FDT on the bench
evidence_words.code: read in the firmware source, not seen on a device

read_as_why: A version on a side branch is looked up as the version it was built on.

capabilities.says: SET_FILTER 0x1C sets the stream rate per plate and the device low-pass; RAM only, a reset restores the default.
Frames per second per plate when no host sent SET_FILTER.
Frames per second per plate when no host sent SET_FILTER; Studio resets the FDT at each start and gets this.
Not in this firmware.
SET_TARE during a stream answers at once; NACK 8 means the plates were not steady, try again, the old zero is kept.
Not in this firmware.
GET_STATUS carries a battery level 0-100 on an FDT with the voltage divider (one bench FDT so far); others send 255.
The FDT switches the pads off and sleeps this long after the last host command; a running stream never sleeps.
The FDT switches the pads off and sleeps this long after the last host command; a running stream never sleeps. Asleep, the Bluetooth bridge is off too.
Not in this firmware.

After a wake, START, GET_CURRENT_CONFIG and SET_TARE outside a stream wait until the pads are ready (about 4.6 s measured, at most 6 s); GET_STATUS, GET_FW_VERSION, KEEP_ALIVE and STOP answer at once.
Not in this firmware.
Noise on the USB line no longer ends the sleep; only a complete host command does, and the reason is logged.
Not in this firmware.
Studio's exam start (START, reset 23 ms later, settings, START) works right after the FDT slept.
No sync modes: start on trigger and event frames come with 1.2.8.24 (contract K1).

SET_SYNC_MODE 0x28 and GET_SYNC_MODE 0x29: start or stop on the SYNC IN jack, SYNC OUT high or pulsing while streaming, and 24-byte event frames in the stream (plate address 0xFD, code 0x0E). Probe with GET_SYNC_MODE: older firmware and the digital variant answer NACK 7. Mode 0 after power-on behaves as before; the mode survives CONTROLLER_RESET, not power-off. While a START waits for a trigger the FDT does not sleep. First drafted as 1.2.8.21; built on the firmware team's 1.2.8.23, and 1.2.8.21 to 1.2.8.23 have no sync. Not yet run on hardware. A second firmware line (four platforms) also used the numbers 1.2.8.24 and 1.2.8.25 for builds without this, so on those two numbers a host must probe rather than trust the version. Draft firmware, not released.
A force or moment beyond the int16 range wraps around to the other sign, so an overloaded plate can read as a small or negative value.

A force or moment beyond the int16 range is held at the limit (32767 or -32768) instead of wrapping; a value at the limit means the channel was overloaded. A second firmware line (four platforms) also used the numbers 1.2.8.24 and 1.2.8.25 for builds without this, so on those two numbers a host must probe rather than trust the version. Draft firmware, not released.
Analog outputs wrap around beyond full scale, and a double plate's analog moments are 100 times too large.
Analog outputs stop at full scale instead of wrapping, and a double plate's analog moments equal the digital ones (before: 100 times too large).
Plate addresses 1 and 2; the FDT ignores plates 3 and 4.

Plate addresses 1 to 4, one or two pads each; the FDT still waits for two plates at start-up and adds a higher plate that answers. Only plates 1 and 2 drive the analog outputs. The four-platform line had four plates from its own 1.2.8.24, so on 1.2.8.24 and 1.2.8.25 count the plates in the stream. Draft firmware, not released.
Not in this firmware: two plates at most.
With four plates, 1000 frames/s per plate is the most the host link carries with 0 lost; 2000/s loses about 22 % (link 150 of 192 kB/s) without stalling. Draft firmware, not released.
Not in this firmware: two plates at most.

A START right after a reset streams after about 2.4 s with four plates. The four-platform line's 1.2.8.25 was silent about 21 s here (a zero per late plate), which is also how Studio starts an exam, so a host that waits 8 s for the first frame fails on it. Draft firmware, not released.
Not in this firmware: a clipped load cell is not reported.

In clip-event mode (SET_SYNC_MODE 0x28) the FDT sends a SATURATION event frame with detail bit 0x40 when a pad reading comes within 2 % of the int16 limit, for pad 2.8 and 2.9 alike; a host turns the mode on before START and puts mode 0 back after STOP. Draft firmware, not released.
The watchdog runs only during a trial boot, so a hang stays silent until a power cycle.

A hang ends in a reset within about 8 s (5.5 s at the fastest clock) instead of silence: a host sees the stream stop and the FDT answer again after its boot. The keep-alive sleep keeps it fed (3.5 min asleep without a reset, measured). Draft firmware, not released.
